questions.prompt: The service restarts after correcting the unit, but no new events appear in FortiSIEM. Which test separates the next stages?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSIEM|The service restarts after correcting the unit, but no new events appear

options.text: Increase the systemd restart delay only
options.feedback: The process is now restarting; a delay does not prove registration or event forwarding.

options.text: Reinstall the agent before checking HTTPS
options.feedback: A reinstall is premature until the outbound Supervisor and Collector channels are tested.

options.text: Disable the monitoring template update channel
options.feedback: The template channel is required for current monitoring configuration and is not a fix for missing events.

options.text: Check Supervisor registration and Collector forwarding separately
options.feedback: The agent registers and receives templates from the Supervisor, then forwards events to Collectors; each channel needs independent verification.

questions.prompt: A Linux Agent installation fails on a host where rsyslog is stopped. What is the first corrective action?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSIEM|A Linux Agent installation fails on a host where rsyslog is stopped. Wha

options.text: Change the Collector address to the Supervisor
options.feedback: Changing destinations does not satisfy the host's local package and logging prerequisites.

options.text: Disable auditd and logrotate on the host
options.feedback: Those components are listed among required packages for supported Linux distributions.

options.text: Start rsyslog and install required packages
options.feedback: The FortiSIEM Linux Agent installation guide lists rsyslog and OS-specific packages as prerequisites.

options.text: Increase the agent's memory allocation
options.feedback: The documented baseline is modest; a missing prerequisite service is the immediate issue.

questions.prompt: The agent is registered to the Supervisor, but monitoring templates never update. Which channel should be investigated?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSIEM|The agent is registered to the Supervisor, but monitoring templates neve

options.text: Check Supervisor registration and template delivery
options.feedback: Template updates are delivered from the Supervisor over the agent's outbound HTTPS control channel.

options.text: Check the Collector event index first
options.feedback: The Collector receives events; it is not the source of monitoring-template updates.

options.text: Restart the host to refresh the template
options.feedback: A reboot does not identify whether the Supervisor control channel is delivering templates.

options.text: Change the RADIUS policy on the Supervisor
options.feedback: RADIUS policy is unrelated to FortiSIEM agent template delivery.

questions.prompt: The process is alive and templates are current, but the Collector shows no new events. Where should the investigation move?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSIEM|The process is alive and templates are current, but the Collector shows

options.text: Recreate the Supervisor device record
options.feedback: The existing registration is healthy, so rebuilding it is not the first step.

options.text: Trace the agent-to-Collector event channel
options.feedback: Supervisor registration can be healthy while the separate event-forwarding channel is blocked or misdirected.

options.text: Increase the agent heartbeat interval
options.feedback: Heartbeat timing does not prove the event channel is delivering records.

options.text: Disable the Linux audit subsystem
options.feedback: Audit data may be one source of events; disabling it would reduce telemetry rather than fix forwarding.

questions.prompt: A new domain-joined laptop is off-network and has never cached a user's AD credentials. Which connection enables the first login?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSASE|A new domain-joined laptop is off-network and has never cached a user's

options.text: Enter cached user credentials manually at sign-in
options.feedback: The scenario states there are no cached credentials yet, which is why pre-logon connectivity is needed.

options.text: Use the user SAML tunnel before login
options.feedback: The normal user tunnel requires the user authentication context that is not yet available.

options.text: Use a machine-certificate pre-logon tunnel
options.feedback: Pre-logon uses the machine certificate to reach AD before the user has logged into Windows.

options.text: Join the laptop to a public Wi-Fi portal
options.feedback: Internet access alone does not create the private path to the corporate AD domain controller.

questions.prompt: After the user completes the first Windows login, what should happen to the pre-logon tunnel?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSASE|After the user completes the first Windows login, what should happen to

options.text: The pre-logon tunnel becomes the user tunnel
options.feedback: The machine-authenticated tunnel is not simply converted into the user's authenticated session.

options.text: The machine certificate remains the user identity
options.feedback: The machine certificate establishes pre-logon connectivity; the user tunnel has its own authentication state.

options.text: The endpoint must keep both tunnels active
options.feedback: The architecture describes pre-logon teardown after login, not permanent dual-tunnel operation.

options.text: The pre-logon tunnel disconnects after login
options.feedback: The documented sequence tears down the temporary machine tunnel after the user signs in, then uses the user tunnel.

questions.prompt: A Windows endpoint repeatedly prompts for SAML credentials despite successful pre-logon domain login. What should be checked?
questions.question_fingerprint: FortiSASE|A Windows endpoint repeatedly prompts for SAML credentials despite succe

options.text: Increase the FortiSASE tunnel idle timeout
options.feedback: Idle timeout does not make the IdP issue a persistent SAML session.

options.text: Replace the machine certificate with a user cert
options.feedback: The machine certificate solved pre-logon AD reachability; the repeated prompt is in the later user SAML flow.

options.text: Disable SAML and force password caching locally
options.feedback: This changes the authentication design and does not address the documented IdP persistence dependency.

options.text: Configure persistent sessions at the IdP
options.feedback: FortiClient's SAML remember-password behavior depends on IdP persistent sessions; pre-logon success does not provide SAML persistence.

questions.prompt: An engineer wants OAuth autoconnect on a macOS endpoint using a non-Entra IdP. Is this supported by the cited architecture?

options.text: Enable OAuth for every IdP and endpoint type

options.text: Use OAuth for macOS IPsec tunnels only
options.feedback: The cited limitation specifies Windows and SSL-based tunnels, not macOS IPsec.

options.text: Limit OAuth to Entra ID on Windows SSL tunnels
options.feedback: The guide limits OAuth tunnel support to Entra ID, Windows endpoints and SSL-based tunnels.

options.text: Replace SAML with a certificate-based machine identity
options.feedback: Machine certificate pre-logon is a separate state and does not expand OAuth user-tunnel support.

questions.prompt: A new spoke receives an unexpected tunnel address before BGP forms. Which object should be inspected first?

options.text: Change the BGP keepalive timer on both peers
options.feedback: BGP timers do not correct an unexpected address allocated before the adjacency is formed.

options.feedback: The orchestrator uses overlay-tunnel-block-ipam to allocate the tunnel address from the configured IPAM pool.

options.text: Increase the SD-WAN SLA latency threshold
options.feedback: SLA thresholds steer traffic after paths exist and do not assign overlay interface addresses.

options.text: Rebuild the IPsec phase-one proposal list
options.feedback: A proposal mismatch affects IKE negotiation, not the source of the configured tunnel IP.

options.feedback: The documented orchestrator workflow requires the correct Fabric root/hub role and does not work when VDOM mode is enabled.

options.text: Change the spoke BGP router ID first
options.feedback: BGP router IDs do not control whether the orchestrator feature is available.

options.text: Disable IPsec auto-negotiate on all spokes
options.feedback: Tunnel negotiation settings do not remove the documented VDOM-mode limitation.

options.text: Move the hub into a different SD-WAN zone

questions.prompt: IKE is up but the expected BGP adjacency is absent on a new spoke. Which generated state should be verified before changing BGP policy?

options.text: Change BGP route-map local preference first
options.feedback: Route-map preference affects route selection after the BGP session is established.

options.text: Verify IPAM loopback and tunnel addresses first
options.feedback: The orchestrator allocates the routing identities from IPAM pools; wrong addresses can make downstream routing appear broken.

options.text: Increase the IPsec DPD retry count
options.feedback: DPD affects peer liveness, not the overlay interface address assignment.

options.text: Change the SLA probe protocol to TCP
options.feedback: SLA probe type does not correct the loopback or tunnel address used by BGP.
